name: AgenticCart – Sell in ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini for WooCommerce
author: agenticcart

sections.description:
Shoppers ask ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini what to buy. AgenticCart puts your WooCommerce catalog there: it prepares every product for AI assistants – the right category, real attributes, a clear summary – and delivers it where shoppers ask.

  • Your own app in ChatGPT and Claude. Your store gets its own MCP server on your AI domain, such as ai.yourbrand.com, published under your name as an app in ChatGPT and a connector in Claude.
  • Product feeds for Google Shopping, Gemini and ChatGPT. A Google feed for Google Shopping, AI Mode and Gemini, and a feed in OpenAI’s format for ChatGPT shopping, which OpenAI admits stores to.
  • An AI storefront on your own domain, such as chat.yourbrand.com, which you can also show in your shop as a shopping assistant.
  • Checkout in your shop. Shoppers fill a cart in the conversation and pay in your WooCommerce checkout, and your AgenticCart reports show the revenue each AI assistant brings.

This plugin is the WooCommerce side of AgenticCart. It syncs your catalog, carries the cart into your checkout and reports the orders AI assistants brought in. The AI, the feeds and the dashboard run on AgenticCart’s servers, so an AgenticCart account is required. See “External services” below for exactly what that involves.

What the plugin does

  • Catalog sync. Bulk-syncs products, variations, attributes, images, categories and stock to your AgenticCart integration, then keeps them current as you edit them in WooCommerce.
  • Store profile. Sends the store settings the storefront needs to present you correctly: shop name and URL, currency, weight and dimension units, country and business address fields, and your terms, privacy and returns page URLs.
  • Storefront actions. When a shopper asks the storefront to save a product, add it to the cart or prepare checkout, the plugin performs the requested action in WooCommerce and hands the shopper back to your store.
  • One-click checkout. When a shopper checks out from the AgenticCart storefront, the whole cart arrives in your WooCommerce cart and the shopper lands on your checkout. WooCommerce computes prices, tax, shipping and stock as usual; payment happens in your store.
  • Revenue per AI assistant. Orders that came through AgenticCart, or that WooCommerce’s own order attribution traces to an AI assistant, are reported so your AgenticCart reports show revenue per assistant and channel. Other orders are never sent.
  • Better product data in your own shop (optional). Product facts AgenticCart’s AI found in your product data – colour, material, pattern, size, gender, age group, brand – plus an SEO meta description and a short description can be written back into your products, so Google for WooCommerce, your shop search and search engines use them too. Only after you switch it on and approve it in your AgenticCart dashboard, only into fields that are still empty, and every change can be undone. Titles, descriptions, GTINs, prices and images are never changed.
  • Shopping assistant on your site (optional). A switch on the settings page adds the AgenticCart assistant to your store’s pages as a small launcher. It is off until you turn it on and is never shown on the cart or checkout page.
  • Background processing. Large catalogs sync in batches through a background job, with progress shown in the WordPress admin, so a sync never depends on a browser tab staying open.

What you need

An AgenticCart account and an API key from your AgenticCart dashboard. WooCommerce 8.0 or newer must be installed and active.

External services

This plugin connects your site to AgenticCart, a hosted service operated by AgenticCart (agenticcart.ai). The connection is not optional: without it there is no storefront to sync to, and the plugin has no function.

All requests go to https://agenticcart.ai over HTTPS. Depending on the request, the plugin authenticates with the one-time connect code, API key, or integration token stored on your site.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you deliberately connect your store (using a one-time connect code or API key): your site URL and domain, your WordPress and WooCommerce version numbers, the plugin version, and your store profile – shop name, shop URL, currency, weight and dimension units, country, business address, city, postal code, and the URLs of your terms, privacy and returns pages.
  • Immediately after connecting: a sample of up to 24 published products, plus your total product and variant counts, so the service can show you a working preview of your storefront before you sync the whole catalog. The sample carries the same product fields as a full sync.
  • When your catalog syncs (on a full sync you start, and when you add, edit, delete or restock a product): your product data – titles, descriptions, prices, SKUs, stock levels, images, categories, attributes and variations.
  • When a shopper uses the storefront: the signed storefront stream key and requesting origin are sent to authorize the action. For the event record, the plugin sends the storefront’s pseudonymous session identifier, product ID and title, quantity, action source, store URL and what happened. No shopper name, email address, postal address or payment detail is sent by this plugin.
  • When a shopper arrives from the storefront’s checkout: the single-use checkout ticket from the link and your integration token, to receive the product IDs and quantities to put in the WooCommerce cart. The ticket is valid for 15 minutes and works once.
  • When an order AgenticCart brought in is paid, refunded or cancelled (in the background, never during checkout): only orders checked out from an AgenticCart cart, or traced by WooCommerce’s order attribution to an AI assistant such as chatgpt.com or perplexity.ai. Sent: order id and number, status, currency, totals and refunded amount, line items (product and variation id, quantity, line total), the order date, the checkout ticket’s hash, and the attribution source type, utm source and medium and the referrer’s host name. No name, e-mail address, postal address, phone number or payment detail.
  • Every 15 minutes and when you press “Apply now”, only if you approved write-back in your AgenticCart dashboard (switch it off under AgenticCart > Settings): the plugin asks AgenticCart for approved product data and then reports, per value, whether it was written, skipped because the field was already filled, or failed. Sent: the AgenticCart ids of these values, the result, the attribute name used and an error text. Received: product ids and the values to write (attribute name and value, brand, SEO meta description, short description). No customer or order data.
  • When you turn on the shopping assistant (and then at most once a day while an administrator uses the admin): your integration token and site URL, to receive the assistant’s public embed token. While it is on, your store’s pages load the assistant script from https://agenticcart.ai/chat.js, and the conversation runs in an AgenticCart frame: what a shopper types there goes to AgenticCart, as on the hosted storefront.
  • When your subscription is verified (on a schedule, and when you save the settings page): your API key, site URL and domain, version information, and the same store-profile fields described above.

The plugin sends no data until a store administrator deliberately enters a connect code or API key. It sends no visitor data beyond what is listed above.

  • Service: https://agenticcart.ai
  • Terms of service: https://agenticcart.ai/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://agenticcart.ai/privacy

Privacy

For logged-in shoppers, the plugin stores wishlist product IDs in the agenticcart_wishlist user-meta field. For guests, wishlist IDs are stored in the WooCommerce session and follow WooCommerce’s session lifetime. Public storefront actions also create short-lived local rate-limit transients containing HMAC fingerprints of the source IP address and signed stream key; the limiter does not store the raw values.

The logged-in wishlist is included in WordPress personal-data exports and removed by WordPress personal-data erasure requests. Uninstall removes all logged-in wishlist metadata and plugin-owned local data. The plugin also supplies editable disclosure text in Settings > Privacy for inclusion in the site’s privacy policy. See “External services” above for the data sent to AgenticCart and the service privacy-policy link.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce must already be active.
  2. Open AgenticCart in the WordPress admin menu.
  3. Enter the one-time connect code from AgenticCart onboarding to pair the store.
  4. Enter the API key from your AgenticCart dashboard and save. The first full catalog sync starts automatically; later full syncs can be started from the Sync screen.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AgenticCart account?

Yes. The plugin is a connector to a hosted service; on its own it has nothing to sync to. Creating an account and connecting a store is free to try – see agenticcart.ai for current plans.

How do my products get into ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini?

Through AgenticCart, once your catalog has synced: ChatGPT and Claude through your store’s own app, an MCP server on your AI domain; Gemini and Google Shopping through a Google product feed you add in Google Merchant Center; and ChatGPT shopping through a feed in OpenAI’s format, which OpenAI admits stores to. Any shopper can also use your AI storefront on your own domain.

Do shoppers pay inside ChatGPT?

No. Shoppers fill a cart in the conversation and arrive in your WooCommerce checkout with the whole cart. WooCommerce computes prices, tax, shipping and stock as usual, and payment happens in your store.

What happens to my product data?

It is stored in your AgenticCart integration and used to answer shopper questions about your catalog. The exact fields are listed under “External services” above, and the handling is described in the privacy policy linked there.

What shopper information does the plugin send?

Storefront events carry a pseudonymous storefront session identifier and the product/action details listed under “External services,” not direct customer identities. Checkout stays in WooCommerce, and the plugin does not transmit shopper names, addresses, email addresses or payment details.

Does it work with product variations?

Yes. Variations sync as their own records with their attributes, prices and stock, so the storefront can answer questions about a specific size or colour.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating stops all syncing and outbound requests and unschedules plugin jobs. Deleting the plugin removes its options, scheduled jobs, update transient, short-lived local rate-limit records and logged-in wishlist user metadata from your site. Data already held by AgenticCart is managed from your AgenticCart dashboard.

My catalog is large. Will a sync time out?

No. Syncs run in batches through a background job with progress reported in the admin, so they continue after you navigate away.

2.8.6

  • Copies installed from agenticcart.ai now get their updates from WordPress.org, like every other install.
  • No change in what the plugin does.

2.8.5

  • No change in what the plugin does.

Versions before 2.8.4 were distributed directly from agenticcart.ai.
